page.layout: One page of text in one column of verse, with the running head at the top right and the page number at the top left. Below the poem: "I. I. B." on its own line, then "POCILLI" in capitals, right-aligned. A dagger mark stands at the lower left. No margin notes.

p.i: Et quos lacteolo pinguior vbere Vates Gallia nutriit. Verum perpetua si Sapientia Facundo referat iura recondita Ore, & si placidis coetibus indicat Qua coelum petitur via: Illi mella fluunt aemula nectari, Sacro digna sonat rite silentio, Et qua vulgus amat, turbaque doctior Intentis bibit auribus. Sic mirata suum Gracia Nestorem Olim densa humeris dulciloquum audiit: Quum verba eximiis picta leporibus Cano pectore promeret. Sic mirata frequens audiit Herculem Prisci temporibus Gallia Celticum, Aures quum domitas duceret aureis Victrix lingua catenulis. Sic Musis niteas Beza fauentibus Semper conspicuo vertice clarior, Et nomen meritis laudibus inclitum Cunctis Gentibus inferas. Maiorem invidia te petat invidus, Ceu Cygnum streperis vocibus anseres, Et ceu quum rabidus Lunam ululatibus Noctiurnus canis impetit.

page.notes: The dagger mark at the lower left is a printed symbol, not text; it is not transcribed. The long s is read as plain s throughout. Some words are slightly soft in the scan: "pitta" read as "picta", "Beza" as "Beza", "Noctiurnus" as printed. The poem starts mid-piece, so the first paragraph is marked as a continuation. No Greek or Hebrew on this page.
